summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology. Firmware experience across STM32 Cortex-M4 bare-metal C, FreeRTOS, and embedded Linux on NVIDIA Jetson, spanning timer-triggered ADC sampling, interrupt-driven UART, and hand-written I2C drivers. Built electromechanical systems from EAGLE PCB fabrication through real-time control and hardware debugging.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design and PCB fabrication.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Built a gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi over HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID cursor commands in Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter via software calibration.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built a Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a hand-written low-level I2C driver.
Programmed peripherals directly at the register level in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); verified peripheral timing in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a vision-guided pick-and-place system across a distributed pipeline: mobile client, edge server, and a Jetson embedded-Linux plus Arduino controller over WebSockets.
Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability across 10/10 trials at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.
Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors through a TCA9548A I2C mux for contact-aware grasping, using a camera range-gate and a gripper-ToF-triggered close at 25 mm.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop - Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon - National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
